items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I don’t think you really start to play until, you know like young Freddie Hubbard played all kinds of stuff... But a little later man, he really started.

ctx.x: You have any unhappiness with the way jazz is being marketed or annotated or being recorded historically these days? Anything currently going on that’s worrisome to you?

Yeah, we don’t have the blues anymore, Monk. The blues is not an element of jazz anymore. That’s why I say the heart is going out of it. Because the blues comes from the heart. And you’ve got all these guys, they’ve got all the licks, you know they can play licks and make your head swim. But that blues element, because I mean the blues is in some ways like a slower way of living, you know? I mean it’s a dues way man. But everybody has a publicist, and if you’re 19 and you’ve got a great publicist and you can play…
